limitations: MSA and templates were explicitly absent.
Identity, finite coordinates and plausible local bond lengths do not validate the predicted global protein fold or binding pose.
ipTM/pTM/ranking score are structural confidence, not affinity, efficacy or human safety.
The 0.9–2.1 angstrom screen is a broad backbone/organic-bond diagnostic, not a complete stereochemical validation.

top_model_coordinate_comparison.correspondence: Full human P35354 residue IDs1–604; CA atoms only
top_model_coordinate_comparison.interpretation: Distinct numerical coordinate outputs only. This comparison does not assess pose accuracy or compare binding affinity.

ile_template_discrepancy.cause: Application protein bond template used RDKit ILE branch atom naming inconsistent with wwPDB/AF3 naming; all 34 old long-bond warnings per sample were an incorrect CG2–CD1 nonbond. This was not sidechain coordinate distortion.
ile_template_discrepancy.standard_residue_comparison: All 20 named heavy-atom graphs checked; ILE is the only adjacency discrepancy. ARG formal-charge/protonation and guanidinium resonance bond-order representation differs between neutral RDKit and +1 CCD ARG; no adjacency discrepancy.
ile_template_discrepancy.interpretation: Correcting the application bond graph removes false long-bond warnings; low AF3 confidence remains and this does not validate fold, binding, efficacy or safety.
